title: Attitude: Following Too Close & Courtesy
whatItIs: Be considerate and patient with all road users. Anyone can make a mistake, so don't react if someone drives badly.
keyFacts: Driving too close to the vehicle in front (tailgating) is dangerous and intimidating.
If someone pulls out in front of you, hold back and let them get clear. Don't drive close to make a point.
If another driver behaves badly, don't react. Pull over and calm down if you need to.
Be patient with learner, young and older drivers: anyone can make a mistake.
When someone overtakes you, keep a steady course and speed, slowing down if needed to let them pass.

items.title: Keep your distance
items.text: At least two seconds on fast roads, more in the wet. Never drive close to intimidate.

items.title: Stay calm
items.text: Don't answer bad driving with more bad driving. Let it go.

items.title: Be patient
items.text: Learners and older drivers may need more time. Give it to them.

items.title: Let others in
items.text: Make room for merging traffic, and don't block junctions.

a.label: Flashing headlights
points: Never assume it invites you to go

b.label: Holding back to let them out
points: Let them decide when to go

onTheTest.question: A driver pulls out of a junction in front of you, so you have to brake. What should you do?
options: Flash your lights to show your annoyance
Sound your horn and follow closely
Overtake them as soon as you can
onTheTest.why: Hold back and let them get clear. Reacting angrily makes the situation more dangerous for everyone.

traps: Courtesy doesn't mean waving people on: let them decide when it is safe.
Speeding up or driving unpredictably while someone is overtaking you is dangerous.
Don't flash your headlights or sound your horn to intimidate or show annoyance.

Rules 134 and 151 (Merging in turn, slow-moving traffic)
